cards.#1: Evergreen is the Heritage Original, built in what Jones call deluxe vegan leather, and at $215 it is the most expensive version of the bag. The material is the only thing separating it from the $125 Burnt Clay, since the 2.9-lb body and three-way divider underneath are identical.
cards.#2: Espresso comes from Painted Hills, a group Jones say is inspired by the landscape of Eastern Oregon, and it is built in industrial canvas. Canvas takes marks in a way ripstop does not, so the bag will look older than it is inside a season, which at $185 is rather the point.
cards.#3: Burnt Clay is the cheapest way into an Original at $125, and it is the same bag underneath as the $215 one. Jones price the line on material rather than construction, which is why the entry point still carries the three-way divider and the unstructured spine that made the shape.
cards.#4: Navy, red and white is the core Jones colourway, here in water-resistant nylon at $175. It is the one that looks like the old photographs, which for a shape the company has been making since 1971 is most of the reason to buy an Original in the first place.
cards.#5: Moss is the third Painted Hills colour and the second canvas Original in the line, at $185. Canvas will mark and soften with use, so this is the version that ends up looking like it has been somewhere rather than like it came out of a box.
cards.#6: The Utility X is the flagship stand bag — 5.1 lbs, a four-way divider and an insulated cooler pocket built into the body. That pocket is the part that separates it from every other stand bag Jones make. Pageant Blue is the brighter of its two colourways, at $345.
cards.#7: Graystone is a 300d recycled ripstop with a wax-effect coating, and Jones say it develops “a character that is earned, not manufactured.” The claim is doing some work, though the coating does mark and darken with handling. Underneath it is the same $345 Utility X, cooler pocket and all.
cards.#8: The Trouper is the five-way-divider bag in the range, and this is the Heritage version in vegan leather with Kodiak trim at $375. Five ways is more organisation than most walkers need and about right for anyone carrying a full set plus a jacket. It is the most expensive stand bag Jones make.
cards.#9: Olive Gray is the standard Trouper at $315, the same five-way bag in F-35 recycled ripstop rather than vegan leather. Sixty dollars separates it from the Heritage version and all of that sits in the material, which is how Jones price every line they run.
cards.#10: Jones bill the Rover as their lightest stand bag — 4.2 lbs with a three-way divider — which puts it a pound under the Utility X. High Desert is the warmer of its two colourways at $295. The Rover is the stand bag for people who would otherwise be carrying an Original.
cards.#11: The Rover in Graystone puts the wax-effect ripstop on the lightest stand bag Jones build, at $295. It is the best-looking thing they make, and the coating is the reason. Grey with a waxed face reads like waxed cotton without carrying any of the weight.
cards.#12: The Short Course is built for ten clubs and an afternoon, four pounds with a cooler pocket, in navy at $195. Ten clubs is the right number for a nine-hole loop, and the bag is cut small enough that you notice the difference on your shoulder.
cards.#13: Jones scaled the Trouper for ages eight to twelve and kept the four-way divider, in dark green at $185. They did not build a toy version of it. The construction matches the adult bag, and the only thing that changed is the length of the frame the kid carries.
cards.#14: Ecru is the Heritage end of the Players Series at $225, with the structured spine and two-way divider that separate the line from the Original. Ecru on a golf bag shows everything it touches, which is the trade you make for how it looks the day it arrives.
cards.#15: Deep Green is the same Players Series bag at $195, trimmed in Kodiak, the vegan leather Jones use across the Heritage line. Thirty dollars under the Ecru and considerably easier to keep clean. The structured spine is the point, since it stands up where an Original slumps.
cards.#16: The Rider is the only cart bag Jones make and the most expensive thing in the range at $520. Sienna is the warmer of the two colourways. A cart bag sits upright in front of you for four hours and gets looked at the whole time, which is a fair argument for the better colour.
cards.#17: The Rider also comes in the house navy, red and white, at the same $520. It is the same cart bag in the colours the brand has run since the beginning, which for a lot of people is the only version of a Jones bag that counts.
cards.#18: Jones announced the RS in May 2026 and it is the first shoe the company has put its name on, in white with field khaki at $200. Matt Lemman’s line on it: a shoe that “looks and feels like Jones, but performs at the highest level the game demands.”
cards.#19: Gray and olive is the second colourway, and the division of labour is clean: PAYNTR do the sole, Jones do the rest. That is the sensible way for a bag company to enter footwear. Olive is also the version that sits with the rest of the range at $200.
cards.#20: The Passenger Tote is one of five pieces Jones made for BEAMS, in a bronze canvas woven for the Japanese retailer’s fiftieth. At $70 it carries that fabric across the biggest surface in the capsule, which is the reason to take it over the dopp kit.
cards.#21: The dopp kit uses the same bronze canvas from the same BEAMS capsule, at $45. It is the cheapest thing in the collaboration and the piece most likely to leave the golf course, since a dopp kit does the same job wherever you take it.
cards.#22: Jones made the Clockwork Hoodie with Standard Issue, in steel blue at $125. It is the only apparel collaboration they have running, which is notable for a company that otherwise puts its name on hard goods. Steel blue keeps it closer to the bag range than to a logo hoodie.
cards.#23: Lusso Cloud make the slide and Jones co-designed it, which is how a recovery shoe ends up in a colourway called Rocket Swirl. At $80 it is the after-round object in the range and the least serious thing the brand has put its name on. It is also the only other piece of footwear they do.
cards.#24: The Rover in Michigan State dark green is $365, against $295 for the same bag in the standard line. Seventy dollars is what the official licence costs, and the bag underneath is the same 4.2-lb three-way Rover. Buy it for the school or do not buy it.
cards.#25: The Stripeshow is the Original with a stripe run through it, here in Georgia colours and in what Jones call leather-look vinyl, at $210. Vinyl wipes clean, which matters more on a white bag than on anything else in the Campus line. The licence accounts for the price against a $175 nylon Original.
cards.#26: At $410 the Missouri Trouper is the most expensive bag in the Campus line, because it stacks Heritage trim on top of the licence. Onyx with Kodiak is the same combination Jones charge $375 for without a school on it, and the bag is otherwise unchanged.
cards.#27: The Circa ’71 covers are named for the founding year and are the only headcovers Jones make. This is the black one with a sock at $60, which is the version that protects a shaft as well as a head. It is the plainest thing in the accessories line.
cards.#28: Orange is the sockless Circa ’71 at $55, five dollars under the version with a sock. Sockless suits a driver that lives in a bag with a full divider, where the shaft is already separated from everything else. Orange also makes the cover findable in a way black does not.
cards.#29: The A2 puts the Graystone treatment on a backpack, which Jones list as F-35 recycled ripstop with a soft-hand PU face, at $160. It is the same fabric as the Rover, so the pack and the bag will age at the same rate if you carry both.
cards.#30: The Out of Office is the cheapest pack Jones sell at $65 and the least golf-looking thing they make. Wheat with black trim reads as a commuter bag rather than a range bag, which is the point of the name and most of the reason to own it.
cards.#31: The Range Hoodie comes from Forrester’s, the outerwear label Jones own and revived, and their own copy calls it “The original golf outerwear since 1951.” Pageant Blue at $148 puts a 1951 label in the same colour Jones run on the Utility X, which ties the two ends of the range together.
cards.#32: Jones make forty-odd rangefinder pouches, which is a strange number for an accessory, and this is the Heritage-trimmed one in Arizona colours at $77. Heritage trim means Kodiak vegan leather on the edges. Seventy-seven dollars for a pouch is what a school licence does to a small object.

kickers.1: The Original is the shape everything else came from — 2.9 lbs, three-way divider, unstructured spine. Jones claim only to have been making them since 1971, which is a narrower and more defensible thing to say. Prices run $125 to $215 on material alone.
kickers.2: Jones call their stand system patented and say it “remains the gold standard.” All of these are built in F-35 recycled ripstop and rated water resistant, from the four-pound Short Course, sized for ten clubs, up to the Utility X and its insulated cooler pocket.
kickers.3: The Players Series is the Original with a structured spine and a two-way divider instead of three, and Jones say the Olive and Sonoma ripstop is woven from 100% PET single-use bottles. The Rider is the only cart bag they make.
kickers.4: Jones work with more partners than most brands their size. The PAYNTR shoe landed in May 2026 and put the name on footwear for the first time, and the BEAMS capsule marks the Japanese retailer’s fiftieth in a bronze canvas made for it.
kickers.5: Eighteen schools carry an official Jones licence, from Arizona to Wake Forest, and the licence carries a markup. A Trouper is $315 in the standard line and $385 in school colours; a Rider goes from $520 to $555. Know that before you shop.
kickers.6: The Circa ’71 headcovers take their name from the founding year. Forrester’s looks like a collaboration and is nothing of the kind — Jones own the heritage outerwear label and revived it, and their own copy dates it to 1951.
